privacy.metaDescription: What the app stores about you, why, who can see it and for how long.
privacy.title: Privacy policy

controller.title: Who processes your data
controller.p1: The controller is <operatorName></operatorName>, <operatorAddress></operatorAddress>. You can write to <contactEmail></contactEmail> — it is the only address at which anything about this data can be resolved.
controller.p2: The app is one person's non-commercial project. Nothing is sold in it, nothing is advertised, and no data is sold to anybody.

stored.title: What we store about you
stored.account: Account — the e-mail address and name from your Google account. When you sign in we ask Google only for the openid email profile scope. We neither read nor store your Google profile picture.
stored.groupName: Your name and role in a group — you can have a different name in each group: “Miro” for the family, “Miroslav” for colleagues. The role is admin or member.
stored.groups: Groups — the ones you created and the ones you belong to.
stored.wishes: Wishes — the name, description, link and an optional photo, plus which of your groups each wish is visible to.
stored.claims: Reservations — who reserved which wish, and when.
stored.history: Gift history — once a gift is handed over, a record is created holding a copy of both names, the wish's name and description, its link and the group names.

notStored.title: What we don't store
notStored.p1: No payment details, no phone numbers, no addresses. No analytics, no traffic measurement, no error tracking, and no advertising or tracking cookies. The app sends nobody any e-mail.
notStored.p2: Photos are shrunk and re-encoded to WebP in your browser, before they are uploaded, which also discards the location data (EXIF GPS) a phone writes into a photo. What reaches the server no longer carries it.

lawfulBasis.title: Why we process it
lawfulBasis.contract: Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) — the account, memberships, wishes and reservations. Without them the app cannot do the thing you opened it for.
lawfulBasis.legitimate: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) — the immutable gift history. The interest is the other party's: their record should not disappear because you left.

whoSees.title: Who can see your data
whoSees.p1: Your wish is visible only to members of the groups you assigned it to. Groups cannot be searched for, and there is no way to request to join one — an invite link is the only way in.
whoSees.p2: The app will never tell you who reserved a wish of yours — nowhere, and at no point. You do not see reservations on your own list. The secret ends only when the person who bought the gift marks it as handed over to you.
whoSees.p3: For technical reasons the operator has access to the database and to the stored photos. They look at the data only when a fault has to be fixed.

processors.title: Who else we entrust it to
processors.supabase: Supabase — the database, sign-in, photo storage, and broadcasting the “something changed” signal.
processors.google: Google — sign-in. Google processes your data under its own rules.
processors.region: The server region and the legal basis for any transfer outside the EU: <hostingRegion></hostingRegion>.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.p1: Everything below is necessary for the app to work — which is why there is no consent banner. None of it tracks you.
cookies.auth: sb-*-auth-token* and sb-*-code-verifier — your sign-in, and the safe completion of signing in through Google. The access token lasts an hour and is refreshed while you use the app.
cookies.returnTo: wishlist-return-to — ten minutes, not readable by JavaScript. It carries an opened invite across the sign-in and is deleted as soon as it has been used. This is what keeps the invite out of Google's hands.
cookies.locale: wishlist-locale — a year, not readable by JavaScript. It remembers which language you chose in the menu. Until you choose one, the app follows your browser's language and no cookie is set.
cookies.installPrompt: install_prompt_dismissed in local storage — remembers that you dismissed the “add to home screen” prompt.
cookies.p2: Signing in is handled entirely on the server, so no session ever ends up in the browser's local storage.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.p1: The account, memberships, wishes and photos are kept for as long as you have an account. They are deleted when it is closed.
retention.p2: The gift history is the exception. A record of a handed-over gift is immutable and kept permanently, even after an account is closed: the link to the account is removed, but both names, the wish's name and description, its link and the group names remain in it, because they were copied into the record at the moment of handover. This is deliberate — otherwise one person leaving would erase a shared history for the other as well. It cannot be undone.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: You have the right of access to your data, to its rectification and erasure, to portability, to restriction of processing, and the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest.
rights.correction: Rectification — you change your name in a group directly in the app.
rights.erasure: Erasure and everything else — write to . The app has no button for closing an account; it is done by hand. On erasure, the limitation described above for the gift history applies.
rights.p2: If you disagree with how we handle this, you may lodge a complaint with the Office for Personal Data Protection of the Slovak Republic.

children.title: Children
children.p1: An account can only be created by signing in through Google, so who may create one is decided by Google's own age rules. The app itself does not ask for an age.

changes.title: Changes
changes.p1: If these rules change, we will update this page and move the effective date at the top. We will announce a substantial change in the app as well.

terms.metaDescription: The terms the app can be used under, what to expect from it and what not to.
terms.title: Terms of use

about.title: What this is
about.p1: “Prajem si..” is a wish-list app for a family, a team or a circle of friends. Everyone writes down what they'd like; everyone else can quietly pick out a gift, and the owner of the list never finds out.
about.p2: It is run by <operatorName></operatorName>, <operatorAddress></operatorAddress>, contact <contactEmail></contactEmail>. It is free to use and non-commercial. By using the app you agree to these terms.

account.title: Your account
account.p1: The only way to sign in is through Google — there is no other way in. You are responsible for your Google account and for who can get at it.
account.p2: An account that is in no group is an ordinary state. You don't have to join anything until somebody invites you or until you create a group yourself.

groups.title: Groups and invites
groups.invite: An invite link is a key. Whoever opens it joins the group — and with it gets access to every wish in it. Send it only to people you want in there.
groups.validity: A link is good for 24 hours, and only a group's admin can create one.
groups.cap: One account can create at most five groups.
groups.noLeaving: You cannot leave a group yourself. The only way out is to ask an admin to remove you.
groups.admin: A group always has at least one admin, and any admin can delete it.

content.title: What you write and upload
content.p1: You are responsible for the names, descriptions, links and photos you add. You must have the right to use a photo you upload. A photo may be at most 2 MB, in WebP, JPEG or PNG.
content.p2: Do not add anything unlawful or abusive, or anything that infringes other people's rights. Content that breaks this may be removed.

moderation.title: Illegal content and moderation
moderation.p1: If you see content in the app that you believe is unlawful, write to <contactEmail></contactEmail> — which group it is in, whose wish it is, and what your objection is. The operator assesses every such report and replies to the address it came from.
moderation.p2: Moderation is done by one person, by hand. Nothing here scans content automatically, no algorithm decides on a removal, and there is no appeals procedure — there is only the same e-mail address.
moderation.p3: When the operator removes content or closes an account, they tell the person concerned, and give the reason. You can object by replying to that same e-mail, and the route to a court always stays open.

secret.title: The reservation secret, and its limits
secret.p1: You will never see on your own list who reserved what for you. The secret ends only when the person who bought the gift marks it as handed over. No deadline and no operator does it on their behalf.
secret.p2: Three things can nevertheless give it away, and it is only honest to name them:
secret.hole1: A reserved wish cannot be deleted or edited — anybody who tries this on every one of their wishes will learn which are taken. (The app never reveals by whom.)
secret.hole2: The person who bought the gift can spoil the surprise themselves by pressing Given too early.
secret.hole3: Removing a member from a group quietly releases every reservation they held.

history.title: Gift history
history.p1: Marking something “given” cannot be undone. It creates an immutable record which keeps the names and the wish's text as a copy, so it stays readable even when one of you leaves the group, when the group is deleted, or when somebody closes their account. It cannot be reversed.

availability.title: Availability and warranty
availability.p1: The app is one person's project, runs on free services and is administered by hand. There is no team behind it, no on-call rota and no support line.
availability.p2: It is provided “as is”, with no guarantee of continuous availability. It may be unavailable for a while, something may break, or it may one day stop running altogether. Keep your own copy of anything you care about.

liability.title: Limitation of liability
liability.p1: To the extent Slovak law allows, the operator is not liable for damage arising from use of the app — including unavailability, loss of data, a surprise given away, or a gift two people bought.

termination.title: Ending it
termination.p1: You can request that your account be closed at <contactEmail></contactEmail>. The details of what is deleted and what remains are in the <privacy>Privacy policy</privacy>.
termination.p2: The operator may remove an account that breaks these terms.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.p1: These terms may change; the version on this page, with the effective date at the top, is always the one that applies. We will announce a substantial change in the app as well.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: This relationship is governed by the law of the Slovak Republic. The courts of <courtVenue></courtVenue> have jurisdiction over disputes.
